### 2026-10-27 — Coconut Cart Rally: skip carts with blocked driver doors

The continued recovery pass first verified sixteen front/rear approaches around all eight rocks. It then reproduced a separate trap at every rock: the nearest spare could be physically parked with its driver door against the rock, and AI kept trying to enter it even though a clear spare was nearby. All eight baseline cases remained on foot after thirty seconds. The fix was playable in approximately seven minutes, with local validation complete in approximately eighteen minutes. The ongoing goal remains active.

Shared cart eligibility now checks supported driver-door clearance before showing a target or planning an AI approach. The player cannot begin an entry through a rock; a cart becomes available immediately when pushed clear, without a restart. AI chooses the usable spare and completes the existing run and entry animation. The doorway probe reuses one vector rather than cloning for every wall. Controls, kart physics, all course geometry, full-height mounds, sponsors and animation clips are unchanged.

All eight blocked-door scenarios recover in under nine seconds from the wreck, with no falls. A human fixture verifies rejected blocked targeting and entry, immediate eligibility after moving the cart, and completed animated entry. Existing interaction/theft and rock mechanics regressions pass. Both lightweight and full production browser fixtures visibly show the racer bypassing the blocked cart and entering the clear spare, with native/MAX and normal-resolution evidence and no WebGL or browser errors. A full eight-racer production race finishes everyone in 100.20–141.98 seconds with zero falls; real keyboard control, trial restart and containment also pass. Type-check/build/release-size checks pass at 999,456,240 / 1,000,000,000 bytes. No new full-suite run was performed for this focused fix.
